scenario.label: Whether to renew the logistics contract
scenario.brief: The contract with our logistics partner is up in six weeks. Before I open the negotiation I want our side's account of how the year actually went, from the two people who deal with them daily, not the summary I get in the monthly.
scenario.theDecision: Service is genuinely worse - late deliveries went from 4% to 19% - but the cause is our own late order cut-off, which changed in March and nobody told the partner. A right answer stops the renewal conversation being about their performance until our own change is on the table.

people.name: Kwabena Asante
people.truth: He has seen the 19% late figure and is ready to move suppliers. He does not know the order cut-off changed. He signed off the cut-off change in March as part of a warehouse shift and has forgotten it.
people.manner: Decisive, impatient with detail, wants a recommendation. Gives ground when shown a number he did not have.

people.name: Blessing Okafor
people.remit: Warehouse manager. Hands the orders over daily.
people.truth: The cut-off moved from 2pm to 5pm in March when the new picking line went in. The partner's trucks are scheduled against a 2pm handover and have been arriving to a half-packed dock ever since. She raised it twice in the weekly warehouse call and it did not reach the COO. She has the dates.
people.manner: Very specific. Dates, times, names. Slightly frustrated at having said this before.

people.name: Yemi Ojo
people.truth: He talks to the partner weekly. They have complained about the handover time since April and he logged it as "operational noise". He genuinely believed it was an excuse. He has the emails.
people.manner: Diplomatic, tends to soften. Will produce the emails if asked what the partner has actually said.
